evals.name: a design write-up becomes a page
evals.prompt: Write up the buffer redesign so the team can read it without me in the room, and give me something I can link in the channel.
expectations: Produce one self-contained HTML file published to a stable URL
Shape it as a short paper: header, reading guide, parts by audience, numbered sections, footer with evidence and revisions
Give every section, figure, and table an id with its anchor shown beside the title
Run the prose pass with the reader named before publishing

evals.name: a chat summary stays in chat
evals.prompt: Quick summary of where the redesign stands? Two lines is fine.
expectations: Answer in chat
Do not build a page for a two-line status

evals.name: sections numbered by hand
evals.prompt: I inserted a new section 3, so I'm renumbering sections 4 through 12 and every cross-reference. Any faster way?
expectations: Number sections with a CSS counter so an insertion renumbers the rest
Keep figures, tables, and listings numbered by hand in order of appearance across the page
Make cross-references links on stable ids, by number

evals.name: a figure cited as below
evals.prompt: The paragraph says 'see the figure below'. The figure is right there, so that's clear, right?
expectations: Refer to the figure by its number as a link
Explain that a shared anchor or a later edit breaks 'below'

evals.name: a status row that says fixed
evals.prompt: The author pushed fixes for all three review findings, so mark the row approved.
expectations: Mark the row awaiting re-review, not approved
Explain that the author saying it is addressed differs from the reviewer confirming it
Make the four touches together: row cells, row class, as-of stamp, dated footer paragraph
Check the live pull-request state rather than the report

evals.name: a number with no baseline
evals.prompt: The page says the sampler costs 2.3% CPU. Where that came from doesn't matter for readers, does it?
expectations: Name the branch and commit the measurement was taken on
Say that a number with no revision cannot be re-derived

evals.name: a branch link in a citation
evals.prompt: I linked the source line on the main branch so it stays current.
expectations: Use a commit-pinned blob link with the full hash
Explain that a branch link moves and the cited line will not be the line described

evals.name: figure colors baked for safety
evals.prompt: To be safe I'm putting literal hex colors in the inline SVG so it never depends on the page CSS.
expectations: Use the page's tokens for an inlined figure so it follows the theme and matches the prose
Reserve baked ink for a figure shipped as an image
Point at the diagram skills for the rule

evals.name: labels estimated instead of measured
evals.prompt: I sized each SVG label box at eight pixels per character, so nothing should overflow. Ready to publish?
expectations: Measure label fit in a real renderer after the figure edit, with fonts confirmed loaded
Say that character estimates have missed overflows a rendered check found
Fix overflow, crossing, and out-of-bounds findings before publishing

evals.name: white on white in dark mode
evals.prompt: A teammate on dark mode says the cards are unreadable. It looks fine for me.
expectations: Define the full light palette on the root, redefine tokens under both dark blocks, set the body background from a token
Find the color defined only inside a theme block
Check both theme states before publishing

evals.name: a reading guide with advice
evals.prompt: I'll add 'Most readers only need Part I, about 25 minutes total' at the top of the reading guide.
expectations: Give per-part reading times, who reads each part and why, and the numbered sections
Add a quick path naming the summary, key figures and table, and the decision
Drop the total time and the advisory sentence; the reader decides from the summary

evals.name: a wide table in the first part
evals.prompt: The guarantees table in Part I has seven columns: property, what the reader sees, layer, how it's derived, where the contract carries it, how it's built in, how it's verified.
expectations: Keep the property columns in the first part, three or four at most
Move the derivation and verification columns to a twin table in the implementation part that repeats the row labels
Point from the first table's caption to the twin

evals.name: a reference page with no work to track
evals.prompt: This page documents the on-disk format and how the writer and readers use it. There's no implementation plan. Do I still need the progress board and the migration part?
expectations: Drop the progress board and the migration part
Keep the reading guide, numbered sections, shown anchors, pinned citations, and the footer's evidence baseline and revision notes

evals.name: a second copy in the repo
evals.prompt: I'll also commit the HTML to docs/ so it's in version control.
expectations: Keep one source republished to one URL
Name the committed copy as a second source of truth that drifts on the first change

evals.name: another agent's prose pass is adopted
evals.prompt: Codex rewrote the page 25% shorter. Looks good, publishing it.
expectations: Compare before adopting: preformatted blocks and table rows byte-identical, decision terms retained, per-section word counts, fit check, attribution line present
Publish only after the comparison passes

evals.name: conventions are offered as beta
evals.prompt: Our audience is customers, not engineers, and three parts feels wrong for them.
expectations: Treat the parts and reading-time defaults as one team's, open to override
Record the override and its reason through engineering-journal
